text: Edwin Hutchins's concept of distributed cognition holds that the cognitive work of a task such as ship navigation is localized entirely inside the mind of the single most skilled navigator.
explanation: False. Distributed cognition claims the opposite: in Hutchins's study of ship navigation, the cognitive work of position-fixing is spread across navigators, instruments, charts, and communication protocols. The cognitive system is the whole ensemble, not any one individual, which is why the framework challenges cognitive individualism.
